name: Representation and Kernel Modifications
text:
# Representation and Kernel Modifications


## Overview
This family of methods modifies the fundamental [primitive representation](#11838-primitive-representation.md) or the spatial kernel functions used in [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) to address limitations in shape modeling, geometric consistency, and [rendering efficiency](#12180-sorting-and-rendering-pipeline-optimization.md). While standard 3DGS relies on positive, isotropic/anisotropic Gaussians with exponential decay, these variants introduce negative color coefficients, voxel-based scaffolding, tangent-plane constraints, alternative radial basis functions, or [grid-based blur kernels](#14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md). They set themselves apart from sibling methods like [Physical Parameter Optimization](4111-physical-parameter-optimization.md) or [WildGaussians](6064-wildgaussians.md) by altering the mathematical definition of the splat itself rather than just the [optimization schedule](#14063-optimization-schedule.md) or camera model.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate within the differentiable rendering framework of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) [Parent](3761-3d-gaussian-splatting-training.md). They share the following core components:
1.  **Primitive Definition:** Each primitive $i$ is defined by a position $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, a covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), an opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$, and color attributes $\mathbf{c}_i$ (e.g., [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients).
2.  **Rasterization Pipeline:** The rendering process involves projecting 3D primitives to 2D ellipses, sorting them by depth, and accumulating color via [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md). The general accumulation equation for a pixel is:
    $$ C = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i $$
    where $T_i = \prod_{j < i} (1 - \alpha_j)$ is the transmittance, and $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of splats covering the pixel.
3.  **Optimization:** Parameters are optimized using gradient descent to minimize a reconstruction loss (e.g., L1, SSIM) between the rendered image and ground truth.
4.  **Differentiability:** All modifications must preserve the differentiability of the rendering pipeline with respect to the primitive parameters to allow back-propagation.

## Subtopics

### [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) extends the representation by allowing negative color values. It partitions Gaussians into positive ($G_{GS}$) and negative ($G_{-GS}$) subsets. This leverages the "Diff-Gaussian" concept, where the ratio of two Gaussian PDFs can model complex nonlinear structures (e.g., donut shapes) via cancellation effects. It is chosen when high-frequency color transitions or complex shapes require fewer primitives than standard positive Gaussians.

### [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)
[Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md) replaces direct per-Gaussian attribute storage with a [learnable voxel grid](#2159-voxelgrid.md) backbone. Gaussian attributes are derived via interpolation from voxel features through a lightweight neural network. This decouples scene density from the initial SfM point cloud, improving generalization in unobserved regions. It is chosen when sparse initialization leads to poor reconstruction in empty spaces.

### [GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)
[GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md) focuses on geometric consistency by densifying Gaussians on the tangent plane of existing primitives and enforcing smoothness of normals and positions between neighbors. It addresses noisy geometry in standard 3DGS. It is chosen when surface reconstruction quality and geometric smoothness are prioritized over raw photometric fidelity.

### [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)
[DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md) replaces the Gaussian kernel with Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs), such as half-cosine or [inverse multiquadric](#9910-inverse-multiquadric-splatting.md) kernels. It uses a correction factor $\psi$ to approximate the closed-form integration shortcut of Gaussians. It is chosen for faster training convergence and lower memory usage while maintaining visual quality, particularly when non-exponential decay profiles are beneficial.

### [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)
[Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md) replaces MLP-generated blur kernels with a learnable, indexed grid to model spatially-varying blurriness. Pixels are assigned to discrete sharpness groups, allowing expressivity to scale with grid size without additional inference cost. It is chosen for modeling defocus or blur in differentiable rendering without the overhead of per-pixel neural network evaluation.

### Gaussian Shell Maps
Combines CNN-based generators with 3DGS to recreate virtual humans with sophisticated details such as clothing and accessories [S1].

### Gaussian Wrapping
A framework that reinterprets 3D Gaussian primitives as oriented probabilistic surface elements representing geometry only within an oriented half-space, allowing derivation of closed-form occupancy, vacancy, and normal fields for watertight mesh extraction [S2].
- Model surface points with asymmetric primitives where the Gaussian models density decay on the outward-facing side, while the inward-facing side is considered fully occupied [S2].
- Identify geometric gaps where the oriented surface assumption is violated and densify the representation to obtain a watertight shell of oriented primitives [S2].
- Introduce a learnable oriented normal at each Gaussian element and define an adapted attenuation formulation to enable closed-form expressions for normal and occupancy fields [S2].
- Introduce a novel consistency loss and a dedicated [densification strategy](#6234-densification-strategy.md) to enforce Gaussians to wrap the entire surface by closing geometric holes [S2].
- Modify the differentiable rasterizer to output depth as an isosurface of the continuous model [S2].
- Use Primal Adaptive Meshing for Region-of-Interest meshing at arbitrary resolution [S2].

## Background
3D Gaussian Splatting was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [G]. The standard representation uses positive Gaussians with spherical harmonics for color. Subsequent research identified limitations in handling complex shapes, sparse initialization, and geometric consistency. [Negative Gaussian Splatting](#9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) [S1, S2] and [Scaffold-GS](#9186-scaffold-gs.md) [S1] address representation flexibility and initialization sparsity. [GeoGaussian](#9187-geogaussian.md) [S1] and Gaussian Wrapping [S2] focus on [geometric priors](#9395-geometric-priors-and-depth-integration.md) and surface reconstruction. [DARBF-Splatting](#9911-darbf-splatting.md) [S1] explores alternative kernel functions for efficiency. Grid-based blur kernels [S1] address defocus modeling. These methods collectively expand the representational capacity of 3DGS beyond the original exponential Gaussian kernel.
